body:
leo: Quick callout  proposing a 'sample category chooser' in the first-run surface. Instead of a big grid, show compact category chips (Web app, Embeddings, Rerank, CLI) so users can filter samples quickly. Persistent until they complete one sample. Thoughts?
anya: Love it. Helps reduce choice paralysis. Mock shows small caps chips though  need to ensure 14px min for readability.
sam: Agree on size. Also keyboard nav: arrow keys between chips, Enter to apply filter. We should announce the selected filter via aria-live.
olivia: Accessibility nits: contrast on the active chip must be >=4.5:1 for small text, and we need visible focus ring. Don't rely on color alone; include icon or underline.
leo: UX question: chips only filter the sample grid or also reorder by recommended? Maybe make it filter + surface a "Recommended for you" top row.
anya: Reorder is fine but be explicit: header says "Recommended" so it doesn't feel like we hid options. Also add a lightweight tooltip explaining why certain samples are recommended (based on usage or job role).
design-bot: Experiment created: sample_category_chips_v1 (filter-only) vs v2 (filter+recommendations). Metrics: sample_filter_click, sample_run_start, sample_completion.
sec-bot: Security reminder: if we pre-fill sample with API keys or demo tokens, ensure tokens are ephem and documented. Don't store credentials in localStorage.
sam: Good call. Also privacy: chips preference can live in localStorage but respect Do Not Track and org opt-outs. Provide a 'Reset onboarding' action in Help.
olivia: Microcopy options for the chooser header: A) "Pick a sample type" B) "Choose a category to get started" C) "Which sample should we show?". My vote B is clearer.
leo: B works. We'll A/B test with copy B vs A. Track: chooser_impression, chooser_clicks, chooser_restore_from_help.
anya: Mobile: turn chips into a horizontally scrollable pill list (swipe left/right) with accessible names and 44px targets. Tapping a chip should open the filtered grid or a small preview sheet.
sam: Tiny nit: include an explicit "Skip suggestions" control for power users that hides the chooser for the session (not forever). Also provide the permanent "Don't show again" option in Settings.
leo: I'll update the Figma frames with 14px chips, focus states, aria-live regions, and the two experiment copies. Posting in #design today. Scheduling a 5-user hallway test next week. Thanks! :sparkles:
